correctness.rationale: Reconstructed every assertion over all fields K with char(K)!=2, all scalar weights lambda and integer k. As A_{-1}=Ke2 and A_1=Ke1, every even map is diag(a,b) and automatically commutes with alpha. For the Rota–Baxter identity the complete four-basis-pair reduction is a(a+lambda)=0, b(b+lambda)=0, b^2=a(2b+lambda); in a field, lambda=0 forces a=b=0, and lambda!=0 leaves precisely (a,b)=(0,0),(-lambda,-lambda). Nijenhuis reduces to (a-b)^2=0 and hence a=b. Writing s=(-1)^k, centroid reduces to b=sa and a=sb, hence beta=a alpha^k. Averaging reduces to b(a-b)=b(as-b)=ab(s-1)=0: s=+1 yields b=0 or b=a; s=-1 with 2!=0 yields b=0. For F_q (q odd) the two lines intersect at the origin so union size 2q-1. All negative k are covered by alpha^{-1}=alpha; no use of finite experiments to establish arbitrary-field conclusions.

evidence: Bakayoko–Attan Example 1.12 explicitly proposes the example and R=-lambda I as a construction input; Bakayoko–Silvestrov Example 3 reuses it.
The averaging scheme depends on an integer power k of a nontrivial involution; its parity changes the Zariski geometry of solutions from one affine line to the union of two, not merely a relabeling.
All four solution varieties and finite-field cardinalities are exact, not sampled heuristics; the claim does not pretend to classify all Hom-associative color algebras.
value.rationale: A modest but motivated exact structural classification: this is a specifically published two-dimensional Hom-associative color algebra chosen to exemplify a nonzero Rota–Baxter operator and subsequently reused as a construction seed. On this natural reference object, the complete solution varieties for the four named operator classes answer which actual admissible transformations exist; in particular, alpha^k-averaging has one line for odd k but two intersecting lines for even k, while centroid and Nijenhuis remain rigid. The parity boundary and complete geometry can be used when instantiating the published Hom-color operator constructions, and prevent assuming a richer family of compatible RB maps than actually exists. The elementary diagonal-equation calculation by itself is not a broad theorem; credit is confined to the complete first operator profile for the exact literature object and its distinct parity phenomenon.
